newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in late dip on Dow slide.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in late dip on Dow slide.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed earlier gains to close slightly down amid a market weighted by moderate profit-taking spurred by a late downturn on Wall Street, dealers said.
"Mexico was clearly influenced by the Dow, but with some pockets of buying," said Ramon Ruiz, sales trader at the BBV-Latinvest brokerage.

The leading IPC share index ended down 5.63 points, or 0.13 percent, at 4,397.82. Earlier, the IPC had gone as high as 4,414.96 points. Trading volume .TV.MX was lighter than for many recent sessions at 110.2 million shares.
Shares listed by Mexico's two largest financial groups, Bancomer and Banacci, both managed to buck the downward trend on the bourse and gained at brisk trade.
Bancomer gained 6 centavos to 3.95 pesos, while Banacci climbed 55 centavos to 21.90 pesos.
Retailer Elektra shed 3.20 pesos to end at 84.50 pesos, while its ADRs ended off 9/16 to 21-7/16.
Dealers said gains in Cetes rates at Tuesday night's central bank auction also helped trigger selling, because of implied political sensitivity rather than the extra cost of doing business.

"There was enough of a gain on the 28-day issue to indicate political concern," Ruiz said, adding that this maturity was indicative because it would fall due soon after the forthcoming mid-term elections.

Mexico will hold elections on July 6 to renew the entire lower chamber of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, several state governors and the first direct poll for Mexico City mayor in modern history.
